Red Wash Transaction and Operating Record

Document ID: SH-PS-RW-TOR-001 Version: 1.1.0 Decision date: 5 September 2026 Canon effective through: 5 September 2026 Synthetic calibration through: 31 August 2026 Classification: Public synthetic diegetic Owner: Pale Sun operating authority State: LOCKED where stated; all generated company records remain synthetic evidence

1. Authority and evidence doctrine

This record selects the controlling Red Wash transaction and 2026 operating case in the fictional Sable Harbor universe. It does not claim that Red Wash, its counterparties, permits, employees, shipments, or financial results exist in the real world.

Four independent labels must not be collapsed:

  • canon state (LOCKED, PROVISIONAL, OPEN, SUPERSEDED);
  • record origin (PUBLIC_SYNTHETIC_DIEGETIC or EXTERNAL_REALITY_ANCHOR);
  • evidence/model state (DERIVED, SUPPORTED_ESTIMATE, PROVISIONAL_ASSUMPTION, SCENARIO, OPEN, CONFLICT, or SUPERSEDED); and
  • period role (SYNTHETIC_CALIBRATION through August 2026 or MANAGEMENT_FORECAST for September–December 2026).

There is no ACTUAL layer in this package. Locking a fictional case decision does not turn a generated row into a historical actual. Real-world sources constrain the synthetic model; they do not authenticate synthetic company facts.

2. Institutional identity

LOCKED: Pale Sun is Sable Harbor's strategic uranium owner-operator business. Red Wash is its dedicated underground Wyoming uranium operation, held through a dedicated legal operating company. Pale Sun is a lean business layer, not another corporate headquarters. Red Wash is an operation first and a controlled proving ground second.

LOCKED: Red Wash produces natural uranium concentrate/yellowcake reported as U3O8. It neither enriches uranium nor fabricates fuel.

LOCKED: Red Wash Mining, LLC is the Wyoming mine operator. Pale Sun Inc. is its Delaware corporate parent, owned through Sable Harbor Industrial Holdings, Inc. beneath Sable Harbor, LLC. Their books and authority remain distinct.

  • approximately 8.5 million contained pounds U3O8;

This is an internal synthetic acquisition and operating basis. It is not a public S-K 1300 reserve disclosure, a feasibility study, a technical report summary, or a professional opinion about a real mineral property.

Inventory and financial derivation

Production cost and DD&A are incurred measures, not automatic period expense. The released package applies a transparent weighted-average inventory roll-forward to opening inventory, 2026 production, cost of sales, and ending inventory. The currently selected supporting assumptions are $45.00/lb opening cash cost, $5.50/lb opening DD&A, an 18% modeled income-tax rate, and $0.550M other working-capital use. These are SUPPORTED_ESTIMATE scenario inputs, not additional locked historical facts.

The generated statement package and cash-flow bridge are subordinate DERIVED outputs. If they do not reconcile to the operating drivers, the generator must fail rather than force the selected narrative. This release does not claim a separate trial-balance dataset.

The selected DD&A bridge is a MODEL_PROPOSED method supported as a SUPPORTED_ESTIMATE: $42.0M of approved aggregate operating assets plus $8.0M of approved capitalized rehabilitation produces a $50.0M composite modeled basis; 547,400 lb produced divided by 7,820,000 recoverable lb produces a 7.0% units-of-production factor; and $50.0M multiplied by 7.0% produces $3.500M of 2026 DD&A incurred. This simplified composite calculation is not an asset-class purchase-price allocation, an audited GAAP useful-life determination, or tax basis.

LOCKED: The current closure-cost scenario is $25.0M and the acquisition-date accounting ARO is $16.0M. They are different measures. Cole's temporary-stop authority creates an operational disposition; it does not make a claim true. The synthetic 2025 stop record therefore keeps observation, judgment, authority, action, later evidence, and remaining uncertainty separate.

9. ARU/BS&T acquisition and industrial interface

The controlling bridge is SH-PS-RW-LOG-001.

LOCKED boundaries:

  • American Resource Utility (ARU) and Blood, Sweat & Tears Railway (BS&T) had no pre-existing commercial relationship with Red Wash;
  • qualified external carriers serve every 2025 Red Wash movement;
  • a real soft, costly, uneven freight backdrop supports—but does not prove—the fictional carrier-consolidation and lane-allocation event;
  • the resulting scheduling disruption creates delivery risk but no lost 2025 annual sales and no change to 2025 annual revenue;
  • the search begins with replacement carriers, broadens to rail mapping, and the question “Whose line is this?” surfaces ARU/BS&T through operating analysis;
  • at discovery, there is no direct mine connection, suitable secure transload, or demonstrated uranium-specific ARU/BS&T capability;
  • $15.0M is an unbooked ceiling; $8.5M Phase 1 is approved, with $3.25M owned by Red Wash and $5.25M by ARU; and
  • no ARU/BS&T uranium custody or service begins automatically.

Acquisition diligence occurs in November–December 2025. Months 0–3 are confirmatory post-close condition work; months 3–6 cover engineering and approvals. Selected ordinary industrial-input service starts July 7, 2026, after the corresponding synthetic commissioning gates. Months 12–18 remain a future mature-integration review. Mixed external-carrier, truck, transload and rail service remains permissible.

The full ARU/BS&T case is implemented in the industrial successor; direct uranium custody remains OPEN. ARU closes January 7, 2026 after Q4 2025 discovery. The 2025 baseline remains separate from the partial service year and normalized annual plans. See industrial/README.md for sources, registers, reconciliations and the participant corpus.

13. Geographic and funding reconciliation

Red Wash's selected fictional anchor is 42.2200° N, 108.1800° W in Sweetwater County, north of Wamsutter in the Great Divide Basin. The DEM screening elevation is approximately 6,885 ft. Derived drill coordinates use NAD83 / UTM 12N (EPSG:26912), centered on 732,748.781991 m E, 4,678,053.610642 m N. Legacy collar coordinates remain in the archived 1.0 source/build revision. Terrain, geology and resource evidence remain synthetic; a real county boundary does not validate a fictional deposit.

The preserved standalone 2026 inventory model derives $1,522,479 operating cash flow and −$7,477,521 free cash flow after $9,000,000 existing capital spending. The separately authorized $3,250,000 mine interface allocation is additional. The integrated successor includes this capital, the ARO rollforward, modeled reclamation cash, intercompany invoices, external origin linehaul, depreciation and tax effects. The industrial financing ledger funds its cash requirement; equity receipts are financing, never revenue. Future 225,000/300,000-ton cases require explicit daily-capacity and operating-calendar upgrades beyond a 600-ton/day plant.
